scope: Space Slug deployment, mouth, mandatory/optional hunts, ship-initiated attack destiny, defeated-ship disposition and cave restoration.
method: Actual Space Slug deployment and mouth/attack commands in GEMP; controlled Big One/cave/ship positions and ordered Reserve draws. Native fixtures issue real deployment and attack commands with component-only admission.
Full recorded rows are compared; no oracle outcomes are normalized. Native cave restoration explicitly differs from the recorded pinned-engine loop.

GEMP deck helper prepends each argument; assault fixture supplies reverse arguments so attack destiny 6 precedes two zero ferocity draws. Turns advance to the current Battle phase without an unintended earlier hunt.

discrepancies.gemp: After the slug is lost, the cave remains marked as a belly and the engine throws its 5000-actions-without-decision loop guard. Fixture catches only that exact exception after checking the connected-cave branch; production reference source is unchanged.

limitations: Production supports remains false. This is integrated component coverage, not complete Space Slug/card/catalog admission or a new Rules Lab study.

Remaining attack work includes generic creature species/creature-versus-creature, weapon targeting of creatures, general participation/inactive/text-cancellation interactions, target-selected and explicit cave-change response events, and immediate end during nested actions/destiny.

Cave belly contents are lost when the slug is lost. Other leave-play destinations need a separate official-rules/GEMP reconciliation. Planet-only creature habitat loss is pending other creature support.
Landing/takeoff mouth restrictions, Dark-owned slug, repeat limits, loss ordering, general optional actions and saved-state corruption have native tests, beyond the six fresh GEMP observations.

All previously recorded engine/product scope remains required, including complete card/timing/setup/capture/Objectives, transport/navigation/space variants, deck workflows, full CPU/PvP certification, clocks and capacity.
